title: Predicting the Reactivity of Acyclic Silylenes and Germylenes in Hydrogen Activation Using Machine Learning.
summary: The first located result-bearing version was posted on ChemRxiv on 2023-06-26 and used machine-learning regression to predict hydrogen-activation barriers for computed acyclic silylene and germylene structures. A later peer-reviewed version reports experimental checks; those later tests are not attributed to the 2023 preprint. The computational result is limited to the represented structures and calculations. AI role: machine-learning regression over computed molecular structures. The later peer-reviewed version appeared in Advanced Science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany).
ai_technology: Machine-learning regression over computed silylene and germylene structures
organization: Chair of Inorganic Chemistry II, Faculty of Chemistry and Biochemistry, Ruhr-University Bochum, Bochum, Germany.

evidence.tested: ChemRxiv v1 explicitly reports ML regression over computed silylene/germylene structures and hydrogen-activation barrier predictions; the final paper reports experimental checks, so the source-supported computational chemistry result is specific.
evidence.unknown: The computational predictions are restricted to the structures and reaction calculations studied; experimental evidence belongs to the later journal version, not the 2023 preprint.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning regression over computed silylene and germylene structures
